title: Uyunid Emirate
capsule: The Uyunid dynasty was an Arab ruling house of Banu Abd al-Qays tribal origin that controlled the al-Ahsa region of Eastern Arabia from roughly 1077 to 1236. Ali ibn Ahmad al-Uyuni led the revolt that overthrew Qarmatian dominance of the region around 1077–1078 with Seljuq military assistance, establishing an emirate centred on Hajar (modern al-Ahsa). At their zenith the Uyunids controlled Bahrain, the pearl-fishing economy of the Persian Gulf littoral, and trade routes connecting Iraq and the Gulf. The dynasty was extinguished around 1236 when the Usfurid tribe displaced them, ending approximately 160 years of Uyunid control over one of the Gulf's most economically productive territories.
